Polynomial-time unit-job scheduling
                   for every fixed number of machines m ≥ 3
                             Human contributor: entered at deposit
                            15 November 2026         Version 1       CC0 1.0

Theorem B (Theorem 8.5 of the checked return). For m ≥ 3, every full schedule of the padded
job set J, |J| = mT , admits a description hierarchy as in Definition 2.9. The root has its one-leaf
description J, every other node has a global description of at most 12m + 25 leaves, and every
marked original-time prefix has a relative description of at most 6m + 16 leaves, independently of
depth.

Credit and search. The construction follows OpenAI [P, Sections 2–9] and the course [L, lessons
1–8]. The exact scope of drbh’s four-machine code is credited in the source record; its Lean build
was not replayed in this audit. The search of 15 November 2026 covered arXiv, STOC, FOCS,
SODA, ICALP, IPCO, ESA, APPROX, authors’ pages, GitHub, the general web and Hexagon,
including citations and title searches for [P]. It found [D], [J] and [G]; no fixed-m ≥ 4 hardness

5.2    Runs and a capacity witness
A run is a chain along a branch with a fixed tag, starting at the root or at a child created by a
switched update, and proceeding only through same-side updates. Its initial entries are the root
entry or the two entries of its initial switch pair. Every other entry is descended from an injection
appended during the run.

Before pruning, a newly appended list may have m + 3 entries. Every carry used in the
estimates below comes from a pruned list and contains at most m injections and at most two
initial entries.
